head.re: Made-up test memo on a late-payment charge under the Example Tax Act
head.scope: Fabricated act, court, rates and amounts — test data only

summary.conclusion: A late-payment charge of KRW 330,000 is due on KRW 10,000,000 of unpaid tax.
summary.basis: It is a fixed charge of KRW 300,000 plus a daily charge of KRW 30,000 for 30 days.[^a10][^a11]

summary.conclusion: If payment slips to 60 days, the charge rises to KRW 360,000.
summary.basis: The daily charge keeps running at KRW 1,000 a day until the tax is paid.[^a11]

summary.conclusion: A reduction to KRW 180,000 is possible only on application.
summary.basis: The office may halve the fixed charge where the taxpayer applies in time, and the Example Court reads that deadline strictly.[^a12][^c1]

question: Is a late-payment charge due when tax of KRW 10,000,000 is paid 30 days after the deadline, and how much?

short_answer.conditions: This holds if the unpaid tax was KRW 10,000,000, payment was 30 days late, the shortfall was not an under-reporting, and no reduction has been granted.

facts: Tax due under the Example Tax Act: KRW 10,000,000.

facts.text: Payment was made 30 days after the deadline.
The return itself was correct; only the payment was late.
No reduction has been applied for.
The taxpayer is not a small taxpayer under the act.

analysis.heading: The amount is a late-payment charge, not an under-reporting penalty
analysis.rule: A late-payment charge applies where a correctly reported tax is paid late; an under-reporting penalty applies where the reported tax is too low.[^a9] The Example Court keeps the two apart.[^c1]
analysis.application: The return is assumed to be correct and only the payment was late.
analysis.conclusion: Only the late-payment charge is in point.
analysis.confirm: Whether the reported amount matched the final assessment.

analysis.heading: A charge arises once the deadline passes unpaid
analysis.rule: Tax not paid by the deadline attracts a late-payment charge from the following day.[^a10]
analysis.application: The tax was paid 30 days after the deadline.
analysis.conclusion: A charge is due for 30 days.

analysis.heading: The charge is a fixed 3 percent plus 0.01 percent a day
analysis.rule: The charge is 3 percent of the unpaid tax plus 0.01 percent of the unpaid tax for each day of delay.[^a11]
analysis.application: 3 percent of KRW 10,000,000 is KRW 300,000, and 0.01 percent a day for 30 days is KRW 30,000.

analysis.heading: A reduction needs an application within the period
analysis.rule: The office may halve the fixed charge where the taxpayer applies within the period set by the act.[^a12]
analysis.application: No application has been made on the facts given.
analysis.conclusion: No reduction applies unless an application is filed in time.
analysis.confirm: The application deadline and whether the delay had a cause the act recognises.

analysis.heading: No further charge accrues on the charge itself
analysis.rule: A late-payment charge is not itself subject to a further charge.[^a13]
analysis.application: The KRW 330,000 is paid together with the tax.
analysis.conclusion: Nothing is added on top of the charge.

calculation.note: All figures are made up for test purposes.

risks.why: The daily charge depends on the exact payment date.[^a11]
risks.check: The bank record of the payment date.

risks.why: An under-reporting penalty follows different rules.[^a9]
risks.check: The return against the final assessment.

risks.why: The fixed charge could be halved if an application is still possible.[^a12]
risks.check: Whether the application period is still open.

risks.why: The Example Court allowed a reduction only for causes listed in the act.[^c1]
A small taxpayer pays the daily charge only.
risks.check: The size test in the act.

risks.why: Every rate and amount here is fabricated test data.

next_steps.action: Confirm the payment date from the bank record.
Decide whether to apply for the reduction.
Pay the charge together with the tax.
